label: Lewis and Clark in Montana
adaptation_note: Eight linked Montana views preserve the 1805 and 1806 distinction, return branch graph and Marias loop, with modern rivers and the two pass/one portage identifiers in separate registered layers. Fine source meanders are explicitly generalised for native navigation; exact date-by-segment or explorer-by-segment attribution beyond the retained source is not invented. Place codes require their external IDs/key; no state-outline or full Divide identity is claimed.
acceptance_requirement: Retain dates, branch connections and direction; do not merge distinct itineraries merely to keep three original panels.

frames.title: 1805 outward regional overview
frames.teaching_key: 1805 outward Montana segment: begin on the east/right of the upper long route, follow westward and then through the southwest bends toward the west/left endpoint. One selected outward itinerary; bends are not separate stopping places. The following western detail enlarges the same path. Short source meanders are generalised within 0.7 native pin for this navigation overview. North up. Uniform scale 0.044 native pins per source unit; centred layout focus (110, 140, 1240, 590). No kilometre scale is inferred from these introduced projected coordinates. Features continuing across a viewport edge are not termini.

frames.title: Pass and Great Falls location-code layer
frames.teaching_key: Same viewport/scale as preceding river layer, north up. Upper-right large circle is the Great Falls portage-region locator. Upper-left small hollow diamond is USGS named-pass identifier 801055; lower-left small hollow diamond is identifier 384568. Two pass codes and one portage-region code only. These retain the source coordinates, with enlarged symbolic radii (1 and 2 native pins), not pass/mountain/region extents. Use the registered river layer for relationships; no full Continental Divide or Montana boundary is drawn.
